item.title: No boats, no aircraft to deliver 500 tonnes of relief to North Fly
item.description: The National Government is working on establishing a National Emergency Authority, to properly coordinate and work assisting disaster affected communities across the country. Minister for Disaster Services Dr. Billy Joseph said its [Authority paper] at its final stages and ready to be brought before cabinet.
item.content:encoded:
The National Government is working on establishing a National Emergency Authority, to properly coordinate and work assisting disaster affected communities across the country.

Minister for Disaster Services Dr. Billy Joseph said its [Authority paper] at its final stages and ready to be brought before cabinet.

“We will bring it to Parliament to make sure that we have a fully established National Emergency Authority in this country, just like in Australia, New Zealand, and even in the United States.”

Dr Joseph was responding to questions from North Fly MP, James Donald in Parliament on the lack of a national disaster response system and the possibility of a state of emergency declaration for this El Nino period.

“What is the National Government's long-term strategic plan to establish a permanent, fully funded and well-equipped National Disaster Response Unit with dedicated assets such as aircraft, buses and other emergency response equipment to ensure that Papua New Guinea can respond swiftly and effectively to disaster anywhere in the country?

Our people deserve a disaster response system that is prepared before a crisis strikes, not one that struggles to respond after lives and livelihoods have already been lost or affected,” Donald said.

Donald said PNG is a disaster prone country and despite this, the national response is largely reactive rather than proactive.

He gave the example of his province, where he is yet to distribute 500 tonnes of relief supplies to his people.

“In my province, fires are happening, rivers are drying up, ships cannot move and there are no supplies.

"The people of Western Province have no water to drink, they are looking for water to cook and the most affected are those in my district. We are running out of fuel because no ship is able to move these supplies. Our only means of survival is through air.

"I have been trying to supply 500 tonnes of relief supplies to my people. To my embarrassment, there is no barge, there is no aircraft, no nothing, because I can't bring in the supplies into the district, only through air. Fly River has dried up and it's very serious. This is a serious catastrophe,” Donald said.

At this stage, the National Government is not considering the declaration of a state of emergency to deal with the El Nino crisis experienced across the country.

item.title: K80 million Papua LNG forum cost questioned in Parliament
item.description: Parliament has been told that K80 million was spent hosting the recent Papua LNG Development Forum in Port Moresby. Finance Minister Thomas Opa confirmed that this was part of the K112 million ceiling, approved by the National Executive Council.
item.content:encoded:
Parliament has been told that K80 million was spent hosting the recent Papua LNG Development Forum in Port Moresby.

Finance Minister Thomas Opa confirmed that this was part of the K112 million ceiling, approved by the National Executive Council.

But Opposition Leader James Nomane questioned how the funds were disbursed, following reports that some landowners had missed out on allowances and accommodation

The recent Papua LNG development Forum, brought more than one thousand landowners from Gulf and Central Province , along with state agencies and stakeholders.

However, the cost of hosting the forum was under spotlight in parliament today.

Opposition Leader James Nomane questioned the allocation of the millions of kina to the forum at a time, when the country is facing the impacts of El nino.

He also raised concerns over reports that some landowners missed out on allowances, accommodation and meals.

Responding to the questions, Finance Minister Thomas Opa confirmed that of the K112 million approved by Cabinet, about K80 million had been spent on the meeting.

He said the forum had resulted in Gulf and Central Province agreeing for a 80 -20 benefit sharing arrangement.

However, the Opposition Leader demanded how the funds was disbursed, which received backing from East Sepik Governor seeking further clarification on how the K80 million was spent.

Minister Opa maintained that the forum was necessary to progress the Papua LNG project towards a Final Investment Decision.

He assured parliament that the National Petroleum Authority would provide a report on the outcome of the forum , including a funding breakup.

item.title: De Belin fired up for first rugby league world cup with Kumuls
item.description: Papua New Guinea Kumuls lock Jack de Belin is ready to make his Rugby League World Cup debut when the home side take on Lebanon at the Santos National Football Stadium this Saturday. The 35-year-old says representing PNG and his family heritage makes this year’s campaign special, as he prepares to run out for his first World Cup after four years with the Kumuls.
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea Kumuls lock Jack de Belin is ready to make his Rugby League World Cup debut when the home side take on Lebanon at the Santos National Football Stadium this Saturday.

The 35-year-old says representing PNG and his family heritage makes this year’s campaign special, as he prepares to run out for his first World Cup after four years with the Kumuls.

Kumul No. 314 is familiar with playing in front of passionate home crowds, but says the opportunity to represent his PNG heritage on the World Cup stage is a significant milestone.

De Belin has family connections to PNG through his grandmother, while his father was born in East New Britain. He says he is looking forward to representing his family in the tournament.

He made his Kumuls debut against the Cook Islands when PNG hosted the 2023 Pacific Championships in Port Moresby.

“This is my fourth year [with the Kumuls], I joined just after the previous World Cup.

“It's been awesome, I've loved the footy team, the culture and the country. Been welcomed with Open Arms to play footy here is special.

“I get to represent my dad and my family in this World Cup.”

De Belin has made 270 NRL appearances, including 252 for the St George Illawarra Dragons before joining the Parramatta Eels, where he made 18 appearances this season.

He said the focus in camp has been on staying positive ahead of the Kumuls’ opening match.

With less than two days before kick-off, De Belin said preparations had been positive, with a mix of players coming off seasons in the NRL, Queensland Cup and Super League.

“It's all about being positive and keeping up with the young boys, who are really proactive. The squad inside the JD's [Jason Demetriou] pick is awesome.

“There's a lot of local talent from Q-Cup and NRL including players from the Super League. We’ve got a wide variety and we’re ready to go,” de Belin said.

He will also be joined by Parramatta Eels teammate Luca Moretti, who is set to make his Kumuls and World Cup debut.

Meanwhile, Lebanon’s Cedars will be led by Wests Tigers prop Alex Twal in their opening-round clash against PNG. The visiting side arrived in Port Moresby today ahead of the match.

item.title: Madang records 60 new HIV positive cases between July-September
item.description: Madang Province has recorded 60 new HIV positive cases in the last three months, July- September, 2026. A report presented by Idinad Clinic at a two- days stakeholders' consultation, which concluded today, clinician Health Extension Officer (HEO), Lissie Wapip revealed the 60 cases were recorded in the third quarter of this year.
item.content:encoded:
Madang Province has recorded 60 new HIV positive cases in the last three months, July- September, 2026.

A report presented by Idinad Clinic at a two- days stakeholders' consultation, which concluded today, clinician Health Extension Officer (HEO), Lissie Wapip revealed the 60 cases were recorded in the third quarter of this year.

She said a total of 1, 956 tests were carried out between July and September, 68% of which were females and 32% males.

Twenty- four (24) of the positive cases were reported at Idinad Clinic whilst the others came through different referral pathways, including the ante- clinic.

HEO Wapip said a lot of the positive cases continue to come through the ante- natal clinic.

Last year, Madang conducted 11, 653 HIV tests, of which 212 cases came out positive.

Of the total tests conducted last year, 2 951 were referrals from the Ante-natal clinics (ANC) Fourteen cases from the ANC returned positive results. This is 0.5 % of the total referrals from the ANC.

On the national scale, an estimated 130, 000 people are living with HIV, with a national prevalence rate of 1.5%. In 2025, an estimated 11, 000 people acquired HIV and 3, 100 died from AIDS- related illnesses.

According to PNG's HIV Fact Sheet, 2026; HIV testing increased from 91, 151 in 2021 to 388, 425 in 2025, resulting in more than 11, 000 HIV diagnoses.

HIV has been reported in all provinces, with a national positivity rate of 2. 9% and provincial rates ranging from 1.0% to 7.6%, reflecting marked geographic variation.

Globally, new HIV infections have declined by 42% since 2010. PNG, however; continues to record around 30 new HIV infections every day, including 7 babies acquiring HIV through mother- to- child transmission.

Although 62, 607 people are receiving anti- retroviral therapy (ART), treatment coverage remains below the estimated number of people living with HIV, underscoring the need to expand testing, treatment and retention in care.

The stakeholders consultation in the last two days was a lead- up to last night's signing of a Memorandum of Agreement by the National AIDS Council Secretariat (NACS), the Department of Provincial and Local Level Government Affairs, the six district development authorities (DDAs), and the Madang Provincial Health Authority to collaborate in HIV prevention and coordination.

Acting Director of the National AIDS Council Secretariat, Michelle Nilkare, said her team is going around the provinces to see how best NACS can connect back to the province.

Madang is the 5th province to sign the MOA after West New Britain, Enga, Simbu, and Western provinces.

item.title: Bogia cocoa farmers receive chocolate bonus
item.description: A group of cocoa farmers from Madang's Bogia District have received the 'Chocolate Bonus' for this year for producing high-quality cocoa beans and meeting the export volume. Chocolate Bonus is a community reward initiative, implemented by Kamapim Limited, a subsidiary of Envirium Group (Belgium), and is registered as a foreign entity in Papua New Guinea.
item.content:encoded:
A group of cocoa farmers from Madang's Bogia District have received the 'Chocolate Bonus' for this year for producing high-quality cocoa beans and meeting the export volume.

Chocolate Bonus is a community reward initiative, implemented by Kamapim Limited, a subsidiary of Envirium Group (Belgium), and is registered as a foreign entity in Papua New Guinea.

The farmers are from Bom and Suaru communities in ward 5 of the Almami Local Level Government area.

Since commencing operations in Madang Province in 2018, Kamapim Limited has been providing training and support to vanilla farmers to produce high-quality vanilla beans for export to premium international markets, particularly in Europe.

The company then expanded its operations into cocoa production; with its first cocoa export registered this year.

Kamapim's General Manager Varun Rai told NBC News that the farmers from Bom and Suaru have met the requirements, and the company is happy to give them the Chocolate Bonus for this year.

He said, "Kamapim is part of Envirium Group, which has an initiative of Chocolate Bonus program based on the supplied volume to the company. We have finalised their project, which is related to water, and we are happy to assist them with their water tank project for the community to fulfil their required needs at the moment."

Tony Joseph, Kamapim's Warehouse and Sourcing Manager, said, "This is our first year to go into cocoa export.

"Besides exporting cocoa, we have also helped Madang Province as a whole by registering cocoa farmers and providing financial literacy training for them.

"Now, we are happy to assist them with the Chocolate Bonus under the company's community engagement program. With El Nino now at its peak, we are happy to help the community with water tanks, which we hope will help them well during this time."

Joseph further explained that the Chocolate Bonus is the premium assistance that the company can give to farmers that supply them with cocoa.

He said Bom and Suaru are the first community to benefit from the project.

As part of the project, Kamapim last week gave two 9000 liters tuffa tanks, water pipes, and taps to the farmers to support them access clean and safe water.

Another incentive that Kamapim Limited is currently working on is a post-harvest facility at Daigul.

Joseph said the facility is a first- of- its- kind in the country, which will allow the company to buy both wet and dry beans from the farmers and process them into quality beans for export.

"The biggest problem we have in the country now is quality, so this facility will help reduce the fermentation burdens on farmers. A lot of farmers cannot afford to build a fermenter because the cost of building one is about K20 to K25, 000.

"Whilst most of them have met the Cocoa Board requirement of owning a hectare of cocoa trees which qualifies them to own a fermenter, they cannot afford to build one.

"Most times, fermenter owners come and sell cocoa beans on behalf of the farmers, and they get a lot of tax from the farmers. We have seen this, and that's why we have come up with the idea to build the post-harvest facility. This will allow the farmers to concentrate on block management and extension of their cocoa farms," he elaborated.

Joseph further stated that a key aspect of their business model is ensuring that farmers receive fair and sustainable benefits for their hard work, and through their international partners, they are implementing the Chocolate Bonus, a community reward initiative based on the supply of quality cocoa beans, and in compliance with the European Union Deforestation Regulation requirements.

The initiative aims to promote sustainable agricultural practices whilst improving community livelihoods.

He said Kamapim is grateful for the strong support provided by the Bom and Suaru community during the past year.

Joseph stated, "Their commitment and contribution has helped secure funding for a community- designed water project."

He also thanked stakeholder partners, Agmark and Farmset for their presence to witness the presentation of the tanks to the farmers last week.

item.title: Imbongu family gives ultimatum over Stanley Kera’s killing
item.description: The family and tribesmen of slain Imbonggu man Stanley Kera have given a seven-day ultimatum to those they accuse of being involved in his killing, demanding that they come forward and take responsibility. Tribal leader and former Kumul Telikom Holdings Limited Managing Director, Jessie Wangua, says the family has repeatedly called on the alleged perpetrators to come forward, including during the
item.content:encoded:
The family and tribesmen of slain Imbonggu man Stanley Kera have given a seven-day ultimatum to those they accuse of being involved in his killing, demanding that they come forward and take responsibility.

Tribal leader and former Kumul Telikom Holdings Limited Managing Director, Jessie Wangua, says the family has repeatedly called on the alleged perpetrators to come forward, including during the late Kera’s haus krai in Port Moresby.

However, he says no one has responded to their calls.

Wangua has specifically called on people from Sugu Valley in Kagua-Erave District of Southern Highlands Province and Purani in Koroba-Kopiago District of Hela Province to address the matter.

He added the people of Imbonggu are peace-loving people who believe in resolving disputes peacefully, describing the killing of their tribesman as barbaric and unacceptable.

“We are a peaceful people who always believe in peace and resolving issues through peaceful means. The killing of our brother, Stanley Kera, is barbaric and unacceptable. He, his family and our tribe had no affiliation with those responsible for his death. We want those involved to come forward and take responsibility.”

Wangua says the family wants the matter resolved through traditional Melanesian reconciliation, but also wants the suspects arrested so police investigations can proceed.

The seven-day ultimatum, which began on Friday, October 9, outlines two demands.

The first is for the two groups named by the family to come forward and resolve the matter through traditional reconciliation, with the family demanding K500,00 and 200 pigs in compensation separately for the alleged perpetrators of Sugu Valley and Purani.

The second is for the suspects to be apprehended and arrested, allowing police to investigate the killing and ensure those responsible face the law.

" We the people of Olgai Welali (OWW) of Imbonggu District and the family of Late Stanley Kera have forward our demand to be resolved through our Melanesian way and that is for the Sugu Valley to compensate K500,000 and 200 live pigs which also goes to the people of Purani that they too must meet the same demand of K500,000 and 200 live pigs."

" an innocent life has been taken for no good reason and for that justice must also be served through the hands of the law and arrest also must be made to the perpetrators," a frustrated Wangua pointed out.

As of Monday, October 12, Wangua says the family had received no response to their demands nor owing up to their wrong doing.

Meanwhile, Minister for Justice and Attorney-General and MP for Imbonnggu Pila Niningi has also condemned the killing, describing it as a tragic loss of a young man with a promising future.

Niningi, who attended the late Kera’s haus krai on Monday 12th October, says Stanley’s life was cut short after he was allegedly mistaken for a tribal enemy.

“It is very unfortunate that a young man with so much potential has lost his life in this manner. His life has been cut short because he was mistaken for a tribal enemy. Those responsible must come forward and face the full force of the law.”

Niningi says he will work with the haus krai committee to help address the matter.

He has called on those allegedly involved to come forward and allow the law to take its course.

Tuesday, October 13, marks the fifth day of the ultimatum, as the people of Olgai Welali in Walume and the late Kera’s family wait for a response.

The family is demanding accountability for Stanley’s death, while calling for traditional reconciliation and police action to address the killing.

item.title: Over one thousand Grade 12 students sit for National Exams in MBP
item.description: A total of 1, 069 grade twelve students are sitting for their National Examinations this week across seven secondary schools in Milne Bay province. ‎Education authorities say the distribution of examination papers and deployment of examination invigilators to respective schools were executed smoothly ahead of the examinations this week.
item.content:encoded:
A total of 1, 069 grade twelve students are sitting for their National Examinations this week across seven secondary schools in Milne Bay province.

‎Education authorities say the distribution of examination papers and deployment of examination invigilators to respective schools were executed smoothly ahead of the examinations this week.

‎Milne Bay Provincial Education Principal Advisor, Roma Tuidam says the divisions priority this week is to ensure the safe delivery of examination papers and the timely arrival of invigilators at examination rooms.

‎‎"Our priority at this point in time is to ensure that the security of the exam papers are being moved from this office to our respective schools and ensuring that exam room protocols are observed at all times.” Tuidam said.

‎‎Meanwhile, 2, 517 grade 10 students from across thirteen schools in the province sat for their national examination last week, while 4, 525 grade eight students are expected to sit for their national Examinations next week from October 19- 22.

‎Tuidam said most grade 10 examination papers have already been returned to the Education Division in Alotau, with papers from remote schools yet to arrive this week alongside their respective invigilators. The Gr. 10 examination papers are scheduled to be marked next week in Alotau.

item.title: Middle Fly first in southern region to submit 2025 DSIP report
item.description: Middle Fly District in Western Province has set a benchmark for accountability and compliance, becoming the 8th district nationally and the 1st in the Southern Region to submit its 2025 District Services Improvement Program Reports through the Digital Bilum Platform. District Administrator and Chief Executive Officer of the Middle Fly District Development Authority, Petrus Malongim, formally submi
item.content:encoded:
Middle Fly District in Western Province has set a benchmark for accountability and compliance, becoming the 8th district nationally and the 1st in the Southern Region to submit its 2025 District Services Improvement Program Reports through the Digital Bilum Platform.

District Administrator and Chief Executive Officer of the Middle Fly District Development Authority, Petrus Malongim, formally submitted the district's acquittals to the Secretary for the Department of Implementation and Rural Development, Aihi Vaki, via the Bilum Online Platform in Port Moresby on Monday

Malongim said the achievement reflects the commitment of his small team to embrace digital transformation for transparency and accountability.

"Our new district status, skeleton capacity and limited facilities are not limitations, but motivation for us to press on and ensure we comply with national reporting requirements," Malongim said.

Middle Fly Open MP, Maso Hewabi, who was present to support the submission, said he is proud of his district's achievement.

"Being the first District from Southern Region and eight in the country despite being very remote and a new district, we are proud to join other districts to rise to that level. Us being new and remote should not be an excuse when it comes to being accountable as stewards of the people of Middle Fly. Their money must be accounted holistically," MP Hewabi said.

Hewabi said the main challenge was logistics and inaccessibility in collecting reports, but his team overcame it by creating a Contractors WhatsApp Group where contractors provide weekly progressive updates.

"With this, our reporting and acquittal is very, very simple," he said.

He said the compliance will now allow the DDA to track past spending and plan future projects better in terms of sectors and locations.

MP Hewabi commended his administration staff for working in unity despite operating on a skeleton structure.

"I have a great team not because of quantity but their strength is unity and respect for each other. I thank DA Mr Petrus Malongim, DFM Mr Kewo Kapala and electoral staff for working together," he said.

He urged other districts to embrace the platform, saying it is user-friendly.

"I urge every district to comply. We all have our own challenges, but this should not be an excuse. It's 51 years of our country. Let's migrate into this new digital platform," Hewabi said.

Hewabi added that his next priorities are to establish an Electronic Transfer System for the District Treasury, build district administration infrastructure to boost staffing, and improve communication services across Lake Murray, Nomad, Strickland-Bosavi and surrounding areas.

The Bilum Platform is an online system used by DIRD to receive and manage acquittals for funds allocated to provinces and districts across the country.
